# AbstractCode

> An agentic coding assistant with two clients — a Rust terminal application
> (`tui/`, crates.io `abstractcode`) and a TypeScript browser application
> (`web/`, npm `@abstractframework/code`). Neither runs the coding agent: it
> runs durably on AbstractGateway, and both clients observe and steer it over
> HTTP and SSE. A session is portable between them.

This file follows the `llms.txt` manifest format (curated links). Use `llms.txt`
when you can fetch the linked files, and `llms-full.txt` when you need one
offline snapshot of the documentation. Regenerate the latter with
`python scripts/generate_llms_full.py`. Format reference: https://llmstxt.org/

Ground rules for reading this repository:

- Status: **pre-alpha**. Interfaces and behavior may change between releases.
- The source of truth is the code, and the executable invariants are the tests
  (`cargo test --workspace` for the terminal client, `npm test` in `web/` for
  the browser client). If the documentation and the code disagree, follow the
  code.
- The two clients release independently: tag `v<version>` publishes the crate,
  tag `web-v<version>` publishes the npm package.
- A reachable AbstractGateway is required. There is no standalone mode.
- Tools are approval-gated by default; approvals are durable gateway commands,
  so a wait raised in one client is answerable from the other.
- The authoritative command list is `/help` inside the terminal client, and
  `abstractcode --help` for the command line.
